fields.Name: IT72 - Queue Engine Lifecycle
fields.Description: Deterministic lifecycle of the MJQueue subsystem (packages/MJQueue) against the real engine loop and the real DB substrate — no LLM calls (the shipped AIActionQueue driver is resolved but never executed). QU1: QueueManager.Config loads the seeded queue-type catalog ('AI Action'/'Entity AI Action') plus the bundle's fixture type from the live DB. QU2: the ClassFactory resolves queue-type names to the shipped drivers, including the priority-1 EntityAIActionQueue subclass chain. QU3: a task fed through the real AddTask/ProcessTasks/StartTask path persists Status=Completed with its Output and frees its concurrency slot. QU4: a failing ProcessTask persists Status=Failed with the JSON-serialized exception. QU5: a THROWING ProcessTask cannot wedge the queue — the slot is freed and a subsequent task on the same queue still completes (the pinned slot-leak fix). QU6: Stop() is idempotent and a stopped queue refuses AddTask. QU7: static AddTask with an unknown type name throws the documented error before any DB write; instance AddTask against an inactive type returns undefined with zero writes. PARKED (requiresEnv RUN_QUEUE_TESTS, unset in CI → reports Skipped): the first CI run proved a real product defect the checks correctly catch — the QueueTask CHECK constraint rejects the column's own 'Pending' default and the nchar(10) Status column truncates 'In Progress', so QueueManager.AddTask cannot persist terminal statuses against the current schema (QU3/QU4/QU5 read the inverse status). Un-gate once the schema is fixed.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Queue types load from the DB, drivers resolve via the ClassFactory, and the real queue loop persists terminal task statuses, survives throwing tasks, and honors stop/negative-path contracts.
